newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr opens firmer amid steady German rates.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr opens firmer amid steady German rates.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger in quiet trade on Thursday at C$1.3809 (US$0.7242). * Dealers said German Bundesbank decision to hold short-term interest rates steady provided a boost for North American currencies. * Currency seen trading in quiet, consolidative manner in today's session amid a lack of significant economic news.

The U.S. dollar rallied to a six-year high against the German mark after the Bundesbank said its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged at its regular policy-making meeting. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady for the next two weeks.

Dealers said that while the Canadian dollar received support from the German decision, the move simply took the unit off overnight lows and did not provide the impetus for a major rally. And lacking any significant economic news, the currency is seen trading in a narrow consolidative range during today's session.

"It really looks like we're in a consolidative range here, probably between C$1.3790 and C$1.3840 until we get some new news. There's still some talk that the Bank of Canada is thinking about raising rates, but it's a lot more talk I think than anything material," the trader said.

The Bank of Canada last hiked interest rates on June 26, the first such increase in more than two years. In raising the key bank rate to 3.5 percent, the central bank said it was attempting to offset weakness in the Canadian dollar.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar firmed against the German mark to 1.3271 marks from 1.3174 marks. The dollar also rose to 83.72 yen from 83.53 yen.
